description: A delay holding two stacks of audio and moving samples between them: whatever is read out of one is written into the other, so the recording is cut apart rather than played back in order

params.text: Latches which stack is being read and which is being written. Out of the box the module reads the second stack and writes the first; pressing this swaps the two round
Latches recording on and off. With a gate at the record override jack the two are combined by exclusive or, so either one alone turns recording on and both together turn it off
Chooses which end of the first stack is read: the upper position takes the oldest sample first and plays it forward, the lower takes the newest and plays it backward
Chooses which end of the second stack is read: the upper position takes the oldest sample first and plays it forward, the lower takes the newest and plays it backward
Scales what is written back into the other stack each time a sample is read out, silent at the far left and unity at the far right
Sets how long the output is faded down and back up around a change of state, up to 20 milliseconds, which is what keeps the switches from clicking
Pressing it exchanges the contents of the two stacks
Sets the rate of the first internal clock, from a sixteenth of a hertz at the far left to a few thousand hertz at the far right; its gate is high for the first half of each cycle
Sets the rate of the second internal clock, over the same range
Chooses which of the two internal clocks swaps the stacks round, clock 1 in the upper position, clock 2 in the lower and neither in the middle
Chooses which of the two internal clocks drives recording, clock 1 in the upper position, clock 2 in the lower and neither in the middle
Chooses which of the two internal clocks empties the stacks, clock 1 in the upper position, clock 2 in the lower and neither in the middle
Chooses which of the two internal clocks exchanges the stacks, clock 1 in the upper position, clock 2 in the lower and neither in the middle
In its upper position the second clock is restarted every time the first one comes round, so the two stay locked together

inputs.text: The audio to be recorded. Nothing at all happens while this jack is empty
A gate here swaps which stack is read and which is written; the select button inverts it. With nothing patched, this jack reads the internal clock chosen by the switch above it
A gate here turns recording on; the record button inverts it. With nothing patched, this jack reads the internal clock chosen by the switch above it
A rise here empties both stacks. With nothing patched, this jack reads the internal clock chosen by the switch above it
A rise here exchanges the contents of the two stacks. With nothing patched, this jack reads the internal clock chosen by the switch above it

outputs.text: The sample read out of whichever stack is currently being read, faded by the smoothing window

notes: The module does nothing whatever until audio is patched: the process routine gives up before touching the stacks when the audio jack is empty
There is no set delay time and no set buffer length. How far back a sample comes from depends on how much has been recorded and how often the two stacks have been swapped
The lamps in the record and select buttons read the second polyphonic channel rather than the first, so with a mono cable patched they stay dark whatever the buttons are doing

inputs.1:
high above 0.1V · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the internal clock chosen beside it; a negative voltage does nothing here.
